messages:
Aisha (PM): Heads-up — ACME pilot requires two non-negotiables for go: SAML SSO + retention-based audit logs. They want pilot in ~4 weeks. Do we ship MVP public without them or delay the pilot?
Tyler (Eng): SAML is ~2w dev + 1w e2e infra work. Audit logs another ~1w. Can parallelize partly but needs 2 engineers full-time.
Jordan (AE): ACME said "must have" for procurement. They can be flexible on start-of-billing if we commit to ship by a date, but legal needs something in contract.
Olivia (Security): For SSO we need account mapping, SCIM or user-sync? Also retention logs must go to customer KMS or secure storage for 180d. Without this, ACME won't sign.
Sam (Design): SSO screens + account mapping UX, 1 designer ~2 days for flows and edge cases. Need decision so I can spike.
Maya (Dir, Product): Proposal: Offer ACME a dedicated pre-release pilot (Dedicated) with a temporary manual onboarding + elevated support while we build full SAML/audit. That keeps public launch on schedule. Thoughts?
Tyler (Eng): Manual onboarding reduces product work but adds ops overhead. Engineering still needs to build audit export and SAML integration in parallel. If we promise full SAML in 3 weeks, we can do it with 2 engs (Tyler + Ravi).
Ravi (Backend): Agree — SAML integration path: use existing oidc/saml lib, deploy auth proxy. Audit logs: add sink to S3 with server-side-encryption + lifecycle. I can scope 2 sprints.
Alex (VP Product): Decision levers: (A) Delay public pilot 3 weeks to include both features, or (B) Keep public pilot, provide ACME dedicated pilot with manual onboarding and SLA credits. We need clear acceptance criteria for either.
Aisha (PM): Acceptance criteria for ACME: SSO functional end-to-end (IdP connect, account mapping), audit logs exported to customer-controlled bucket for >=180d, and smoke tests for RBAC. If we choose (B) we must document manual steps and rollback plan.
Jordan (AE): ACME prefers (A) if timeline is guaranteed. If we commit to date they will sign immediately. If (B) they might accept but will ask for discounts.
Olivia (Security): Also require threat-model review before SAML goes live; add 1 day for security testing.
Tyler (Eng): Rough ETA: SAML (2 engs): 3 weeks dev + 1 week e2e & security = 4 weeks. Audit logs: 1.5 weeks. Parallel -> ~4 weeks total on critical path. If we delay 3 weeks we can include both.
Maya (Dir, Product): Tradeoffs: delaying moves out roadmap items (analytics v2, routing rules) by one sprint. If we do (B) with dedicated pilot we keep roadmap but accept extra contracts work.
Sam (Design): For (B) we should prepare a simplified onboarding flow and an FAQ for AE. I'll have designs for manual invite flow by EOD Thu.
Aisha (PM): I'll draft a short decision doc and run with Eng & Sales. Can we be synced by Mon EOD for final call?
Tyler (Eng): I'll post a quick implementation checklist tomorrow.
Ravi (Backend): I'll open the feature branches and an infra RFC — will ping for review.
Alex (VP Product): Good. If we go with a delay, let's lock down which roadmap items to defer and communicate to Eng. If we do dedicated pilot, specify credits/discounts and ops SLA.
Jordan (AE): I'll negotiate timeline language with ACME contingent on our commit. If we need a firm date I'll ask for a 2-week buffer in the contract.
deploy-bot: Created doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/ssaml-audit-prelaunch (internal) :link:
Aisha (PM): Thanks — will circulate the decision doc in #product and tag everyone. Meeting Mon 10am to decide. :calendar:
Tyler (Eng): :thumbsup:
Olivia (Security): I'll schedule a threat-model slot Mon morning.
Maya (Dir, Product): Agree on Mon 10am.
Jordan (AE): Will have ACME's legal contact ready.
Aisha (PM): Closing thread — please add any blockers to the doc.
